actions.action: Inspect leaf undersides, joints and stem bases with a flashlight for pests
Dab suspicious spots with an alcohol-dipped cotton swab to test if they are pests
If mealybugs or scale are found, wipe them off with alcohol-dipped swabs
Isolate the plant if pests are found
Move the plant a few feet back from the window glass
Alternatively, hang a sheer curtain to diffuse direct sun
Gradually acclimate the plant to brighter light over one to two weeks
Check deeper soil moisture with a finger or wooden skewer
Water thoroughly when the deeper soil is nearly dry
Cut fully brown leaves off at the base
Set up a pebble tray to raise humidity
Alternatively, use a humidifier to raise humidity

reason: The answer leads with light stress and treats pests only as an unconfirmed possibility without naming thrips. Its pest check, alcohol wipe and isolation steps partly cover the fix, but it gives no thrips-specific treatment such as neem or insecticidal soap. It is not harmful because it still tells the owner to confirm there are no pests.
